problem: In any nondegenerate triangle the greater side subtends the greater angle.

proof_idea.original: Cut the greater side to the smaller length, use isosceles base angles and the exterior-angle comparison.
proof_idea.analytic: Strict Lagrange bound and cosine law give a positive factorization of the cosine difference; principal arccos strict decrease gives the angle order.

litex_code:
# Book I.18: a greater triangle side subtends a greater angle.
# Positive lengths and their squares have the same strict order.
thm proposition_18:
    ? forall a, b, c cart(R, R):
        a != b
        a != c
        b != c
        $geometry::main::is_triangle(a, b, c)
        geometry::main::distance_sq(a, c) > geometry::main::distance_sq(a, b)
        =>:
            ray_angle(a, b, c) > ray_angle(a, c, b)
    release thm greater_side_has_smaller_opposite_cosine(a, b, c)
    release thm angle_cosine_bounded(a, b, c)
    release thm angle_cosine_bounded(a, c, b)
    release thm arccos_strictly_decreasing(angles::angle_cosine(a, b, c), angles::angle_cosine(a, c, b))
    ray_angle(a, b, c) = arccos(angles::angle_cosine(a, b, c)) > arccos(angles::angle_cosine(a, c, b)) = ray_angle(a, c, b)
